clue.text: "All shook up" recording previously assigned grade other than A

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record or CD
once means at one time in the past

indicators.note: other than A says the letter A is dropped from the word before it

parts.note: to be rated is to be assigned a grade

explanation.surface: An old Elvis hit gets a mediocre rating the second time round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'other than A' removes A from RATED, leaving RTED. The quoted Elvis title is the definition, taken in its literal sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone thrown off balance and agitated is figuratively shaken up, flustered and unsettled.

clue.text: Higher air is draining when son makes ascent

indicators.note: makes ascent says the son's letter climbs to an earlier spot in this down entry

parts.note: decants means pours off liquid, emptying one vessel

explanation.surface: When a son climbs up, the air is drained.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, rising means moving towards the top, so S moves from the end of DECANTS to sit after DE.
explanation.definitionFit: A melody sung or played above the main tune is a soprano counterpoint, an upper line.

clue.text: Time not recorded in KO? Call timekeeper outside

indicators.note: not recorded says the time letter is missing from the word

parts.note: a knockout punch stuns its victim
to dial is to call on the telephone

explanation.surface: A boxing knockout timed by nobody, so call the timekeeper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not recorded' is the deletion signal. 'Time' and 'timekeeper' sound like boxing, but this timekeeper sits in the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden device showing the hour by a shadow cast in sunlight keeps time out of doors.

clue.text: Protestant marching from mountains in state

indicators.note: in places the mountain word inside the state

parts.note: Oman is a state on the Arabian peninsula
a range is a chain of mountains

explanation.surface: A Protestant marches down from the hills into his home state.
explanation.walkthrough: The Orange Order is a Protestant fraternity in Northern Ireland known for its marching parades.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the Orange Order are Ulster loyalists famed for their annual parades.

clue.text: Perhaps treasury's standing reduced

indicators.note: reduced says the word is shortened by its last letter

parts.note: cachet means prestige or standing

explanation.surface: The Treasury's reputation has taken a knock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced' removes the final T. The 's is 'is', the link; 'Perhaps' shows treasury is an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A hidden store of valuables is one kind of hoard, of which a treasury is an example.

clue.text: Get upset at any time without odd bits of credit

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the time word surrounds the picked letters
upset in a down clue says the word is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: ever means at any time

indicators.note: odd bits of picks the first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: A debtor is always upset at getting no credit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' is a reversal in a down clue; 'without' means outside, not lacking, so the reversed word wraps the odd letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To obtain or be given something is to take delivery of it, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Supply more guards for each ruler

indicators.note: guards says the rearranged letters stand around the each word
supply here is the adverb of supple, flexibly, so the letters bend into a new order

parts.note: per means for each, as in per head

explanation.surface: Supply extra guards for every king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supply' rearranges MORE into EMOR, which 'guards' PER.
explanation.definitionFit: The sovereign of an empire is a monarch, a supreme ruler.

clue.text: Not necessarily notes from the Commons?

definitions.text: Not necessarily notes from the Commons?

parts.words: Not necessarily notes from the Commons?
parts.note: the Commons is a parliamentary chamber, so notes from it would be music from a chamber; it need not be from parliament

explanation.surface: Memos from Parliament are not always what they seem.
explanation.walkthrough: The House of Commons is one chamber of the UK Parliament; 'notes' are musical, not written.
explanation.definitionFit: Classical works for a small ensemble, each part played by one player, suited to a room rather than a hall.

clue.text: Obsolete Asian currency note returned — glory be!

indicators.note: returned says the combined letters are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: the anna was a former coin of India, a sixteenth of a rupee
soh is the fifth note of the tonic sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A collector of old coins delights in an Indian piece coming back with a note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' reverses ANNA + SOH to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are exclamations of praise to God, the one a Hebrew shout of adoration used in worship.

clue.text: Enclosure for driver's mate with depression

parts.note: cock is a familiar form of address, like 'mate', in Cockney speech
a pit is a hollow or depression in the ground

explanation.surface: A driver's friend is suffering from low spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of driver's stands for 'is', linking definition and wordplay; 'mate' and 'depression' look emotional but are a pal and a hole.
explanation.definitionFit: The compartment a racing driver or pilot sits in is an enclosed space for whoever is at the controls.

clue.text: Fancy jumper? Down-and-out musician's disposed of half a dozen

parts.note: a tramp is a homeless vagrant, a down-and-out

indicators.note: disposed of says the six letters are removed from the musician

parts.note: a violinist is a musician
VI is six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A homeless musician has thrown away six fancy sweaters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disposed of' removes VI from VIOLINIST, leaving OLINIST. 'Jumper' is British for a sweater, but here it is one who jumps, fancily.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer who bounces and somersaults on a sprung canvas is an acrobatic leaper.

clue.text: Whining woman judge dismissed in Dynasty

indicators.note: in places the shortened name inside the dynasty

parts.note: the Ming dynasty ruled China from 1368 to 1644

indicators.note: dismissed says the judge's letter is sent away from the name

parts.note: Joan is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A complaining woman judge is thrown off the TV soap Dynasty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dismissed' removes J from JOAN, leaving OAN, which goes 'in' MING.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe complaining in a persistent, plaintive and querulous voice.

clue.text: Retire to redevelop area in country

indicators.note: redevelop asks for the letters of the word before to be rebuilt in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone retires to rebuild a district in some nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to redevelop' rearranges RETIRE into ERITRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Eritrea is a nation in the Horn of Africa, on the Red Sea coast.

clue.text: Applaud former group getting back together

parts.note: ex- means former, as in ex-husband

indicators.note: getting back says the word for a group is turned round

parts.note: a lot is a group or set of things

explanation.surface: Fans cheer an old band reuniting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting back' reverses LOT to TOL; 'together' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: To praise someone enthusiastically is to laud or acclaim them.

clue.text: Working method Pasteur devised for cheese

parts.note: MO is short for modus operandi, a way of working

indicators.note: devised suggests the letters are worked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Louis Pasteur's working method was devised to make cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'devised' rearranges MO + PASTEUR. In Britain this word is slang for cheap, bland cheese, the sort used as bait.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang names cheap mild cheddar after the bait one would put in a trap for rodents.

clue.text: Peacekeepers' groom, you might say, less settled

parts.note: UN peacekeepers serve the United Nations
a groom keeps horses in a stable, so might jokingly be called a stabler

explanation.surface: A peacekeeping groom is rather less settled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'you might say' flags an invented word: one who stables horses.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakier and more wobbly means more precarious, lacking steadiness.

clue.text: Italian family head cut off drugs

parts.note: the Medici were the ruling family of Renaissance Florence

indicators.note: cut off says the final letter of the headland word is removed

parts.note: a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness's neighbour Inverness

explanation.surface: The head of a Florentine dynasty is cut off from his drug supply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut off' trims NESS to NES. 'head' is a geographical headland, not a person's head.
explanation.definitionFit: Medications are substances taken to treat illness, which is one sense of drugs.

clue.text: Humble Democrat agreed to reform

indicators.note: reform says the letters of the word before are re-formed in a new order

explanation.surface: A modest Democrat agrees to change his ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to reform' rearranges AGREED into EGRADE.
explanation.definitionFit: To humble someone is to lower them in dignity, debasing or abasing them.

clue.text: Self-sufficient Scot vacated car more frequently in past

indicators.note: vacated means emptied, so only the outer letters remain

parts.note: ofter is an archaic comparative of oft, meaning more often

explanation.surface: A Highland smallholder used to leave his car empty more often.
explanation.walkthrough: A croft is a small farm in the Scottish Highlands, worked by its tenant for subsistence.
explanation.definitionFit: A Highland smallholder who farms a croft largely to feed the household is self-reliant.

clue.text: Stone section of folly rebuilt when knocked over

indicators.note: when knocked over says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Part of a garden folly is rebuilt after being toppled.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'section of' the two words reads LYREB, which 'when knocked over' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: A precious gem such as emerald or aquamarine is a variety of this mineral, a stone.

clue.text: Elaborate craft? -there's nothing in it

indicators.note: in it places the zero inside the sailing ship

parts.note: a barque is a sailing ship, a craft
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Is fancy handicraft really empty inside?
explanation.walkthrough: 'craft' looks like handiwork but is a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Highly ornate and extravagantly decorated, like seventeenth-century European art and architecture.

clue.text: Shindig in case header's forgotten after game

indicators.note: after puts the shortened case word behind the game

parts.note: RU is rugby union

indicators.note: header's forgotten says the first letter is dropped

parts.note: an action is a legal case

explanation.surface: A rowdy party breaks out after a football match in which a header was missed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'header' sounds like football but means the first letter: ACTION loses A. Shindig here means a noisy row.
explanation.definitionFit: A disturbance or noisy quarrel is a row or commotion, the sense of a rumpus.

clue.text: Clue taken out — end message

parts.note: a sign is a clue or indication
something taken out or removed is off

explanation.surface: A crossword clue is removed, finishing the communication.
explanation.definitionFit: To close a letter or broadcast is to conclude a communication with a final word.

clue.text: Take care of following up American hub

explanation.surface: Following an American hub is something to look after.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses CO to OC; 'Take' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The centre of attention or activity is its focal point, its centre.

clue.text: Father tucked into Ist class preserve from the continent

parts.note: A1 means first-class
Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title
to can food is to preserve it in tins

explanation.surface: A priest tucks into first-class jam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ist' is the printed form of '1st'; A1 is read as AI.
explanation.definitionFit: Something originating on that particular landmass, Africa, is said to be from the continent.

clue.text: Anarchic discussion with old captive in charge

indicators.note: captive says the old letter is held inside the discussion word

parts.note: a chat is an informal discussion

explanation.walkthrough: 'captive' places O inside CHAT, giving CHAOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking any order or control, a state of disorder resembles a land without government.

clue.text: £51 and extra shilling for flowers?

parts.note: 51 in Roman numerals is LI, and a quid is British slang for a pound, so fifty-one pounds is LI quid
S is the abbreviation for a shilling, the old British coin, here added on

explanation.surface: Paying fifty-one pounds and a shilling extra for a bouquet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flowers' is not blooms but things that flow; the question mark flags the pun. A shilling was a pre-decimal British coin, abbreviated S.
explanation.definitionFit: Fluids such as water run freely, so anything that flows can whimsically be called a flower.

clue.text: New money from Brussels to stimulate medic

parts.note: euros are the currency issued by the EU, based in Brussels
